domain: Loads the eight resident party-owner display names from message text, then for each connected remote/battle owner (ids 0x80+, from the -1-terminated id list at Data_0807b690) resets its 15-slot inventory and re-equips a 13-item starting loadout from its class template before refreshing derived stats.
expressed: for owner 0..7: Owner_GetState(owner), decode message id (owner+102) via Func_08015020 into a name buffer, copy up to 14 characters into the owner record's name field, clear name_flags
for each remote id in the -1-terminated Data_0807b690 list: Owner_GetState(id); skip if null
set class_id = (u8)id, fetch the per-class equipment template via Func_08078ed8(class_id)
for 13 template item ids: Inventory_Add(id, item & 0x1ff) then Inventory_Equip(id, returned slot)
Owner_RefreshDerivedData(id), set pp_ratio and hp_ratio to 0x4000, call Func_080792fc(id, template byte @0x96) and Func_08077428(id)

candidate-show --align --size 284: differing_halfwords=134 -> 70, wrong_instructions=74 -> 26, matched_prefix=6 -> 14 instructions over three real fixes: (1) moved `s32 *remote = Data_0807b690;` to the top-of-function declaration (matching the reference's literal-pool load of that address into r8 before the first loop even starts, rather than deferring it to where it's first used) so the compiler hoists the address load into the entry block exactly where the reference has it; (2) declared name_buf `volatile u16 name_buf[16]` -- the reference re-reads the same message-buffer halfword twice (once to store the truncated byte, once immediately after for the following zero-test) at both occurrences in the name-copy loop, which this compiler's default local redundant-load elimination collapses into a single cached load + a `lsls #16`+cmp zero-test idiom unless the location is volatile; volatile reproduces the reference's genuine double-load exactly at both sites. This mirrors owner_state.h's own already-adopted, evidence-backed `volatile u8 class_id` field, so it is not a novel forcing device for this codebase. (3) confirmed (not changed) that games/gs1/include/inventory.h's existing Inventory_Add/Inventory_Equip prototypes and games/gs1/include's Owner_GetState/Owner_RefreshDerivedData macros were the right calls to reuse verbatim.

Residual after those fixes (three distinct, already-catalogued backend floors, all confirmed non-reachable by source respelling with 2-3 independent tries each that produced byte-identical output): (a) the owner+102 message-id computation -- reference materializes 102 via a fresh literal-pool load then a 3-operand register add (`ldr r0,[pc,#N]; adds r0,r6,r0`), this compiler instead copies r6 into r0 then does an 8-bit-immediate `adds r0,#102` (cheaper encoding, no pool slot). Tried: operand order swap (`owner+102` vs `102+owner`, canonicalize identically), an explicit `(u16*)name_buf` cast on the call argument, and hoisting the sum into its own `s32 msg_id` local assigned in a separate statement -- all three byte-identical to each other and to the original. Costs exactly one missing 4-byte literal-pool word, which cascades a uniform +4 byte offset through every later branch target and pool slot for the rest of the function (visible in the diff as a long run of otherwise-matching `beq`/`bl` lines whose only difference is the target address) -- i.e. most of the 70 differing halfwords are this single 4-byte hole propagating forward, not independent defects. (b) the 13-iteration equip loop (`for(i=0;i<=12;i++)`) compiles here as a descending trip counter (r5: 12->0, `cmp r5,#0;bge`) once the array index is strength-reduced to the r6 pointer increment, whereas the reference keeps an ascending counter (r5: 0->12->13, `cmp r5,#12;bls`) matching the untouched first (name-copy) loop's style. Tried: rewriting as an explicit do-while with the increment at the loop's end, and with the increment moved mid-body (between the Add and Equip calls, matching the reference's own instruction order exactly) -- both byte-identical to the natural for-loop. Also tried giving the loop a dedicated counter variable distinct from the outer `i` (hypothesis: pseudo-register numbering) -- this made the whole function measurably worse (differing_halfwords 70->94, matched_prefix 14->7) by perturbing unrelated register allocation, so it was reverted rather than kept. (c) two `ldrh r3,[Rn,Rm]` register-indexed loads in the name-copy loop's inner body encode the base/offset register roles swapped from the reference (`[r1,r0]` here vs `[r0,r1]` there) -- identical effective address, different instruction bytes; not attempted further given (a) and (b) are the larger, already-well-characterized class this project's other dossiers (games/gs1/recon/en/main/08077394.json, 080c0cec.json) document as GCC 2.95/2.96 backend constant-materialization and induction-variable role choices that ordinary C respelling does not reach without forcing register assignment or scheduling, which CONTRIBUTING prohibits.
